==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|id=thing|:der|fro:object>|tree=1}} From {{der|en|fro|object}}, from {{der|en|la-med|obiectum||object|lit=thrown against}}, from {{m|la|obiectus}}, perfect passive participle of {{m|la|obiciō||to throw against}}, from {{prefix|en|ob|gloss1=against|sort=ject}} {{m|la|iaciō||to throw}}, as a calque of {{der|en|grc|ἀντικείμενον}}. {{doublet|en|objectum|objet}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|noun}}: {{enPR|ŏb'jĕkt}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɒb.d͡ʒɛkt/|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/ˈɑb.d͡ʒɛkt/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-object-noun.ogg|a=US}} ** {{rhymes|en|ɒbdʒɛkt|s=2}} * {{a|en|verb}}: {{enPR|əb-jĕkt'}} ** {{IPA|en|/əbˈd͡ʒɛkt/|a=RP,GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-object-verb.ogg|a=US}} ** {{rhymes|en|ɛkt|s=2}} * {{hyph|en|ob|ject}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # A {{l|en|thing}} that has {{l|en|physical}} {{l|en|existence}} but is not alive. # {{l|en|objective|Objective}}; {{l|en|goal}}, {{l|en|end}} or {{l|en|purpose}} of something. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1825|publisher=Great Britain. Parliament. House of Lords|title=Accounts and Papers|page=91 |passage=Money is an '''Object''' to you?
Money is an '''Object''' to me.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1860|author=Thomas Fenner Curtis|title=The Progress of Baptist Principles in the Last Hundred Years|page=161 |passage=And yet it may be proper to show that if time were an '''object''', little, if any thing, would necessarily be gained by sprinkling in place of immersion, where a large number had to be baptized.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1863|author=Great Britain. Parliament. House of Commons|title=Reports from Committees|page=240 |passage={{...}} to secure first-class men you must either hold out a temptation of money, if money is an '''object''' to them, or if it is not, then after a certain number of years' service, perhaps, some honour to be bestowed upon them; one or the other, I think, ought to be given to secure the best men that you can.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1877|author=South Australia. Parliament|title=Proceedings of the Parliament of South Australia: With Copies of Documents Ordered to be Printed ...|page=29 |passage=I think, if a captain had plenty of time to spare, and was not going on to any other port, he would prefer going into harbor; but if time were an '''object''' with him, and he wished to get away as quickly as possible, he would go to the pier outside.}} # {{senseid|en|n-grammar}} {{lb|en|grammar}} The {{l|en|noun phrase}} which is an internal {{l|en|complement}} of a {{l|en|verb phrase}} or a {{l|en|prepositional phrase}}. In a verb phrase with a {{l|en|transitive}} action verb, it is typically the receiver of the action. #: {{hypo|en|direct object|indirect object}} #: {{cot|en|subject|;|agent|patient|rheme|theme}} # A person or thing toward which an emotion is directed. #: {{ux|en|Mary Jane had been the '''object''' of Peter's affection for years.}} #: {{ux|en|The convertible, once the '''object''' of his desire, was now the '''object''' of his hatred.}} #: {{ux|en|Where's your '''object''' of ridicule now?}} ## {{lb|en|chiefly in the negative}} A cause for [[attention]] or [[concern]]. ##: {{syn|en|focus}} ##: {{co|en|the '''object''' of a strongly worded censure}} ##: {{ux|en|Money is no '''object''' to him.}} # {{senseid|en|compsci}} {{lb|en|object-oriented programming}} An {{l|en|instantiation}} of a {{l|en|class}} or {{l|en|structure}}. # {{lb|en|category theory}} An {{l|en|instance}} of one of the two kinds of {{l|en|entities}} that form a {{l|en|category}}, the other kind being the {{l|en|arrow}}s (also called {{l|en|morphism}}s). #: {{ux|en|Similarly, there is a category whose '''objects''' are groups and whose arrows are the homomorphisms from one group to another.}} #
